player_action: I move diagonally three squares. That's 15 feet, right?
correct_ruling: No. Diagonals alternate 5 ft and 10 ft: the first diagonal costs 5, the second 10, the third 5, so three diagonals cost 20 ft.
srd_reference: CombatI.rtf > Movement, Position, and Distance > Measuring Distance > Diagonals

player_action: I move 2 squares through rubble (difficult terrain), straight line.
correct_ruling: Difficult terrain costs 2 squares of movement per square (10 ft per square), so two squares cost 20 ft.
srd_reference: CombatI.rtf > Movement > Moving Through a Square > Difficult Terrain
common_wrong_rulings: Difficult terrain gives a penalty only to attacks.

player_action: I move diagonally through one square of difficult terrain.
game_state: Speed 30, single diagonal move into difficult terrain, first diagonal this move.
correct_ruling: A diagonal into difficult terrain counts as 3 squares (15 ft).

player_action: I'm in the mud. I take a 5-foot step out of it to avoid provoking.
game_state: Fighter stands in difficult terrain (mud), adjacent to an orc.
correct_ruling: You can't take a 5-foot step into or out of difficult terrain? Per the SRD, you can't take a 5-foot step in difficult terrain, so the fighter must take a normal move (which may provoke) or withdraw.
srd_reference: CombatI.rtf > Movement > Difficult Terrain; CombatII.rtf > Take 5-Foot Step
confidence_note: SRD says you can't take a 5-foot step in difficult terrain; whether that covers stepping OUT of difficult terrain into normal terrain is read differently by tables.

player_action: I charge the ogre — I'll go around the table to get to it.
game_state: Barbarian speed 40, ogre 30 ft away, a table blocks the straight line.
correct_ruling: A charge requires moving in a straight line directly toward the target to the closest square from which you can attack, with an unobstructed path. You can't charge around obstacles; the barbarian can't charge here.
common_wrong_rulings: Charge just needs line of sight.

player_action: I charge the goblin. What bonuses and penalties do I get?
game_state: Fighter, goblin 20 ft away in a straight unobstructed line.
correct_ruling: Charging gives +2 on the single melee attack roll and -2 to AC until the start of your next turn. You move up to double speed and must move at least 10 ft.

player_action: I charge the kobold that's 5 feet away.
correct_ruling: You must move at least 10 ft (2 squares) to charge, and must start not already adjacent in a way that allows moving toward the target; from adjacent you can't charge it.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Charge > Movement During a Charge

player_action: I run. How far, and can I run through the rubble?
game_state: Human fighter speed 30, medium armor, light load.
correct_ruling: Running is a full-round action. In medium armor (or heavier) or carrying a medium/heavy load you run at x3 speed; otherwise x4. So 90 ft here. You can't run across difficult terrain, and you lose Dex to AC while running.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Full-Round Actions > Run; CombatI.rtf > Difficult Terrain

player_action: I withdraw from the two orcs I'm fighting.
game_state: Wizard speed 30, threatened by two orcs. No other enemies.
correct_ruling: Withdraw is a full-round action: move up to double speed; the square you start in is not considered threatened by visible enemies, so leaving it doesn't provoke from them. Later squares you pass through that are threatened can still provoke.
common_wrong_rulings: Withdraw prevents all AoOs during the move.

player_action: I withdraw, but I'm invisible-blind — I can't see the second orc.
correct_ruling: Withdraw only protects against visible enemies; invisible (unseen) enemies still get AoOs for leaving the starting square. A blinded character can't see them, so both can still attack.
confidence_note: SRD says invisible enemies still get AoOs; applying that to a blinded withdrawer is a reasonable extension rather than exact text.

player_action: My Medium character squeezes through a 2.5-foot-wide crack while fighting.
game_state: Medium fighter, crack is at least half his space width.
correct_ruling: Squeezing: each square moved costs 2 squares, and while squeezing you take -4 on attack rolls and -4 to AC.
srd_reference: CombatI.rtf > Big and Little Creatures in Combat > Squeezing / Movement > Squeezing

player_action: Rogue and I are on opposite sides of the bugbear. Do we flank?
game_state: Fighter and rogue each adjacent to bugbear on directly opposite sides, both threatening.
correct_ruling: Yes. Flanking gives each a +2 flanking bonus on melee attacks, and the rogue can sneak attack.

player_action: I'm diagonally adjacent to the troll on its northeast; the rogue is directly south. We're flanking, right?
game_state: Troll Large? No: troll is Medium-sized stand-in, 1 square. Fighter NE, rogue S.
correct_ruling: No. Flanking requires a line drawn between the two attackers' centers to pass through opposite sides or opposite corners of the defender's space. NE and S don't satisfy that, so no flank.

player_action: I'm holding a bow at the orc's back while the fighter is opposite. We flank, so +2 for me too?
game_state: Archer adjacent with bow only (no melee weapon, no armor spikes, no Improved Unarmed Strike).
correct_ruling: No. Only a creature that threatens the defender can flank, and ranged weapons don't let you threaten. The archer doesn't help flank and gets no flanking bonus (flanking bonus applies to melee attacks anyway).
common_wrong_rulings: Archers can flank by position alone.

player_action: I move through the ogre's square to get behind it.
game_state: Rogue speed 30, ogre hostile, not helpless.
correct_ruling: You can't move through an enemy's square unless it is helpless, or you use Tumble (DC 25) or overrun. Moving through allies' squares is fine.
srd_reference: CombatI.rtf > Moving Through a Square > Enemy
common_wrong_rulings: Move through enemies at double cost (5e rule).

player_action: I tumble past the guard at half speed to avoid the attack of opportunity.
game_state: Rogue with ranks in Tumble, light armor, speed 30.
correct_ruling: A DC 15 Tumble check lets you move through threatened squares at half speed without provoking (DC increases by 2 per additional opponent). Failure means you provoke normally.

player_action: I drop prone as part of my movement and then stand back up for free.
correct_ruling: Dropping prone is a free action, but standing up from prone is a move action and provokes attacks of opportunity.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Move Actions > Stand up from prone; Free Actions > Drop prone

player_action: I want to swing on the chandelier across the hall and kick the duke.
game_state: Swashbuckler-type rogue, chandelier 20 ft away, no specific rule.
correct_ruling: The SRD has no specific chandelier-swinging rule; it's a DM call, typically resolved with an appropriate check (e.g., Jump, Climb, Tumble, or Dex) and DM-set DC and movement cost.
srd_reference: No specific rule; DM adjudication (Skills: DM sets DCs)
common_wrong_rulings: Claiming a specific swinging rule exists.
